exposure: first pregnancy preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM)
cohort: Women with first deliveries recorded in the Aberdeen Maternity Neonatal Databank, 1986-2005
finding: First pregnancy PPROM was associated with an equal likelihood of second pregnancy but with a significantly increased risk of adverse outcomes in the next singleton pregnancy, including PPROM, PE, instrumental and caesarean delivery, PIH, APH, neonatal infection, neonatal death, admission to neonatal unit, preterm delivery, and LBW.
mod_finding: PPROM in the first pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of instrumental [OR (95% CI): 2.2 (1.7-2.8)] and caesarean delivery [1.8 (1.5-2.3)] in the next pregnancy.
